written: 2026-11-27 (UTC), before scripts/research_v4f.py existed or produced any number on real data
status: Fixed. Not edited after results exist. Hindsight; not part of the ledger; not a forecast.
asked_for: The owner approved a test of a random-matrix measure, the absorption ratio (Kritzman, Li, Page and Rigobon 2011, 'Principal Components as a Measure of Systemic Risk'), computed from US industry returns, as a possible input to the score or a replacement for inputs whose owners restrict commercial use.
what_has_already_been_seen: Round 5 part B tested the average pairwise correlation of the 49 French industries over 63 days. It failed: near highs 0.463 / 0.509 / 0.514 (train / test / 1927-1985) and on all days 0.382 / 0.514. The share of variance on the first eigenvector of a correlation matrix is close to a rescaling of the average correlation, so the prior for the level candidates below is that they fail too. Not seen: any eigenvalue measure, any 500-day window, the standardized shift, anything filtered by the Marchenko-Pastur edge.
data: 49 French industry portfolios, daily, value weighted (the series of round 5). Industries with a missing day inside a window are left out of that window; a day needs at least 20 industries. Market, outcomes, v3 and the bootstrap exactly as in round 5.

outcomes.O1: market closes 10% or more below today's close within 63 trading days

uncertainty: Moving-block bootstrap, 63-day blocks, 2,000 draws, seed 20261134, 90% intervals. Widened for 3 candidates where stated (the 10%/3 percentile).

candidates_and_direction.H1_level: Absorption ratio as in the paper: covariance of daily returns over 500 trading days, exponentially weighted with a 250-day half-life; share of total variance on the largest round(K/5) eigenvalues, K = industries in the window. Higher = riskier.
candidates_and_direction.H2_shift: The paper's signal: (15-day average of H1 minus its 252-day average) divided by the standard deviation of H1 over those 252 days. Higher = riskier.
candidates_and_direction.H3_filtered: Correlation matrix over 252 trading days, equal weights. Share of the eigenvalue sum that lies above the Marchenko-Pastur upper edge (1 + sqrt(K/252))^2. Higher = riskier.

no_tuning: Windows, half-life, number of eigenvectors and the edge are the paper's or the textbook values. No other setting is tried. If a setting has to change for a technical reason it is said in the results.

bars.alone: O1 AUROC on all days at least 0.58 on BOTH train and test and at least 0.55 on 1927-1985, and on the test period the lower end of the interval widened for 3 candidates above 0.50.
bars.in_the_rule: v3 plus the candidate as one more component (levels at its 50th, 75th and 95th percentile of 1990-2006, not counted toward floors) must clear the round 5 part A bar: test O1 at least 0.02 above v3 with the lower end of the difference, widened for 3 candidates, above zero; train not more than 0.02 below; test O2 not more than 0.01 below; ladder rises from Calm to Stress allowing one tie; state changes within 25% of v3. And the clean check: on 1927-1985 the average of the drawdown level (5/10/20) and the candidate's level beats the drawdown level alone with the 90% interval above zero.
bars.price_only: Because of the licensing question. Base = average of the percentile ranks (ranks taken within 1990-2006 values, applied everywhere) of the 252-day drawdown and 21-day realized volatility. Base plus the candidate's rank must beat the base on O1 with the 90% interval of the difference above zero on BOTH the test period and 1927-1985.

reported_whatever_happens: near-high O1 AUROC on all three periods
rank correlation of each candidate with VIX, with v3, with breadth and with round 5's average correlation, 1990 on
v3 plus breadth plus the candidate against v3 plus breadth (round 5b's E1), test period, for information only

reading.propose: A candidate that clears 'alone' and 'in_the_rule': proposed to the owner as a v4 input. The live rule changes only if the owner says so.
reading.replace_inputs: A candidate that clears 'price_only': proposed as part of a price-only score to replace licensed inputs.
reading.record_live: A candidate that clears 'in_the_rule' except the clean check, or 'alone' only: recorded live as a shadow measure like breadth, no rule change.
reading.otherwise: Dropped and published as a failure. No further settings of the same measure are tried.

what_this_cannot_show: Whether anyone pays for it. A measure that passes still has to be explainable on one line on a phone; a measure that fails costs nothing but this record.
